subject: Data capture defaults and exception handling for Acme Payments
messages:
From: David Reynolds <david.r@acmepayments.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 May 2025 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on capture defaults and deletion windows

Hi Vivek,

Quick set of questions from our security & procurement teams as we evaluate Redwood for production: we need a plain-language statement of your default behaviour for the hosted API: specifically:
- What is the default retention window for raw requests (prompts) and model outputs (responses)?
- Are streamed token fragments persisted anywhere if a session is not finalized?
- Does default capture vary by region (we're EU-based, need EU residency) and can you provide erasure/evidence documentation?

We have a short procurement checklist attached (Acme_Retention_Reqs.docx) — would appreciate short answers we can drop into our vendor review. Also please attach any SOC2 / evidence checklist you can share.

Thanks,
David
David Reynolds
Head of Security Operations, Acme Payments

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: David Reynolds <david.r@acmepayments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 May 2025 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on capture defaults and deletion windows

Hi David — thanks for the clear list, and for sending the checklist. Summarizing Redwood's default hosted behaviour below (short, actionable points you can share with procurement):

1) Default capture windows (hosted API):
- Request payloads (prompts / user inputs): retained by default for 60 days. These are used for debugging, rate-limiting analytics, and model quality alerts.
- Model outputs (responses): ephemeral by default and not written to long-term stores unless the customer enables the optional "persist_results" flag. When persisted by configuration, outputs follow the same retention window as requests (60 days) unless otherwise contracted.
- Streaming fragments (partial tokens): treated as ephemeral buffers. If a session is not finalized (no explicit finalize/save), fragments are discarded immediately and are not written to persistent logs.

2) Region / residency:
- For customers on the EU region (eu-west), default storage for captured data remains within EU physical regions. For global accounts using multi-region routing, residency is per-route and documented in the account settings.

3) Deletion & erasure evidence:
- Self-service: account admins can request immediate purge of retained artifacts via the Console -> Data -> Erase. Purge actions generate an audit id and an exportable erasure certificate (PDF).
- Support-driven: for contractual erasure (e.g., 7-day SLA), open a support ticket and we will provide time-stamped proof of deletion (audit id, storage tombstone time, and affected object ids).

4) Sensitive field handling & hashing:
- By default we store raw request payloads (as above). Customers can opt-in to automatic redaction of known sensitive fields via the SDK ("redact_fields" option) or request a data transform at ingest. We can also provide an enterprise-configured pipeline that hashes or tokenizes PII before persistence.

5) Dedicated / Private options:
- For Dedicated (reserved capacity) and Private (VPC/on-prem) customers we can configure shorter retention windows (including contractually enforced 7-day rolling retention) and stricter auto-purge schedules.

I've attached a concise internal playbook excerpt (capture-exceptions-playbook.pdf) and our SOC2-evidence-checklist.pdf for procurement. Happy to hop on a 30-min call if you want to review specifics and API flags.

Best,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Product — Redwood Inference

From: David Reynolds <david.r@acmepayments.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmepayments.com
Date: Thu, 15 May 2025 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on capture defaults and deletion windows

Vivek — thanks, that's helpful. Two follow-ups from our side:

- Can you list exact API flags/SDK configuration names we should reference in our security questionnaire (we need the key names to map into our control matrix)? e.g., is it "persist_results", "redact_fields", etc.?
- Procurement is asking whether Redwood can commit to a 7-day auto-purge for hosted customers under a formal addendum, or whether that capability is strictly for Dedicated/Private deployments.

I've attached our procurement doc so you can mark suggested language. If possible we'd like a short written statement for our vendor review pack.

Thanks,
David

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: David Reynolds <david.r@acmepayments.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 May 2025 17:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on capture defaults and deletion windows

Hi David — Kimberly from Sales here, looping in to confirm options and next steps for contracting.

Short answers you can include in the vendor pack:
- API/SDK configuration names (reference): "persist_results" (boolean, default false), "retain_inputs" (boolean, default true for 60-day capture), "redact_fields" (list of json paths), "auto_purge_days" (account-level setting for Dedicated/Private).
- Hosted customers: our standard hosted offering ships with the 60-day request retention and ephemeral-by-default outputs. We can offer a hosted addendum for enterprise customers that enforces a 7-day auto-purge for captured artifacts; this is a contractual exception (requires legal & security review).
- Dedicated/Private: 7-day rolling retention and custom purge schedules are configurable by default as part of the deployment contract.

Next step: if you send back a redline or proposed language in the attached doc, Marissa (cc'd) will coordinate with Security and Legal to produce a short written statement and an addendum draft. We aim to turn a first-pass statement around within 3 business days for enterprise prospects.

Cheers,
Kimberly Park
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
